knowledge:
- key_parameters: isPaired=Logical indicating whether to run paired or unpaired LIMMA statistical tests ;; cores=Number of threads to accelerate calculations ;; PreSetNumClustVSClust=Number of clusters for VSClust (set to 0 to automatically estimate) ;; PreSetNumClustStand=Number of clusters for standard fuzzy c-means (set to 0 to automatically estimate) ;; maxClust=Maximum number of clusters to evaluate during cluster number estimation ;; scaling=Scaling method applied to data (e.g., "standardize") ;; VSClust=Logical indicating whether to run variance-sensitive clustering (TRUE) or standard fuzzy c-means (FALSE) ;; infosource=The category ID from the STRING API used for functional enrichment (e.g., "KEGG")
- alternatives: Standard fuzzy c-means (FCM) clustering, which can be run by setting VSClust=FALSE in runClustWrapper. Standard FCM is preferred when individual feature variances are not available or when comparing the impact of variance-sensitive clustering.
- when_to_use: Appropriate for multi-dimensional quantitative omics datasets (transcriptomics, proteomics) with replicated measurements across multiple experimental conditions, especially when the number of conditions is large (D > 6) where variance-sensitive clustering shows major improvements.
- pitfalls: Datasets with unequal numbers of replicates per condition must be preprocessed to have the same number of columns per condition (by removing excess replicates or adding empty columns) ;; Input data must follow the sample layout format: A1, B1, C1, ..., A2, B2, C2, ... (where letters are sample types and numbers are replicates) ;; High values of maxClust can drastically increase computation time ;; Functional enrichment via STRING API converts feature IDs without specifying species, which can lead to inconsistencies when using generic gene names.

workflows.name: bioconductor_object_workflow
workflows.intent: Run variance-sensitive clustering on quantitative omics data stored in Bioconductor objects (such as MultiAssayExperiment or SummarizedExperiment).
input: miniACC (MultiAssayExperiment object containing quantitative omics assay data)
workflows.stages: 1. Log-transform and normalize assay data ;; 2. Prepare the Bioconductor object for clustering using PrepareSEForVSClust ;; 3. Estimate the optimal number of clusters using estimClustNum and optimalClustNum ;; 4. Run variance-sensitive clustering using runClustWrapper.
workflows.code:
Experiment <- "miniACC" 
isPaired <- FALSE
cores <- 1 
PreSetNumClustVSClust <- 0 
PreSetNumClustStand <- 0 
maxClust <- 10 

data(miniACC, package="MultiAssayExperiment")
# log-transformation and remove of -Inf values
logminiACC <- log2(assays(miniACC)$RNASeq2GeneNorm)
logminiACC[!is.finite(logminiACC)] <- NA
# normalize to median
logminiACC <- t(t(logminiACC) - apply(logminiACC, 2, median, na.rm=TRUE))

miniACC2 <- c(miniACC, log2rnaseq = logminiACC, mapFrom=1L)

boxplot(logminiACC)

#### running statistical analysis and estimation of individual variances
statOut <- PrepareSEForVSClust(miniACC2, "log2rnaseq", 
                               coldatname = "OncoSign", 
                               isPaired=isPaired, isStat=TRUE)

#### Estimate number of clusters with maxClust as maximum number clusters to run 
#### the estimation with
ClustInd <- estimClustNum(statOut$dat, maxClust=maxClust, cores=cores)

#### Use estimate cluster number or use own
if (PreSetNumClustVSClust == 0)
  PreSetNumClustVSClust <- optimalClustNum(ClustInd)
if (PreSetNumClustStand == 0)
  PreSetNumClustStand <- optimalClustNum(ClustInd, method="FCM")
#### Visualize
  estimClust.plot(ClustInd)

#### Run clustering (VSClust and standard fcm clustering
ClustOut <- runClustWrapper(statOut$dat, 
                            PreSetNumClustVSClust, NULL, 
                            VSClust=TRUE,
                            cores=cores)
Bestcl <- ClustOut$Bestcl
VSClust_cl <- Bestcl

workflows.name: standard_matrix_workflow
workflows.intent: Run variance-sensitive clustering on standard quantitative omics data matrices with replicates, followed by functional enrichment analysis.
input: protein_expressions (Data frame or matrix containing quantitative feature values across replicated conditions)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare the data matrix and estimate individual feature variances using PrepareForVSClust ;; 2. Estimate the optimal number of clusters using estimClustNum and optimalClustNum ;; 3. Run variance-sensitive clustering using runClustWrapper ;; 4. Perform functional enrichment analysis on the resulting clusters using runFuncEnrich.
workflows.code:
library(vsclust)
Experiment <- "ProtExample" 
NumReps <- 3  
NumCond <- 4  
isPaired <- FALSE
cores <- 1 
PreSetNumClustVSClust <- 0 
PreSetNumClustStand <- 0 
maxClust <- 10 

data(protein_expressions)
dat <- protein_expressions

#### running statistical analysis and estimation of individual variances
statOut <- PrepareForVSClust(dat, NumReps, NumCond, isPaired, TRUE)

dat <- statOut$dat
Sds <- dat[,ncol(dat)]
cat(paste("Features:",nrow(dat),"\nMissing values:",
            sum(is.na(dat)),"\nMedian standard deviations:",
            round(median(Sds,na.rm=TRUE),digits=3)))

## Write output into file 
write.csv(statOut$statFileOut,
          paste("",Experiment,"statFileOut.csv",sep=""))

#### Estimate number of clusters with maxClust as maximum number clusters 
#### to run the estimation with
ClustInd <- estimClustNum(dat, maxClust=maxClust, scaling="standardize", cores=cores)

#### Use estimate cluster number or use own
if (PreSetNumClustVSClust == 0)
  PreSetNumClustVSClust <- optimalClustNum(ClustInd)
if (PreSetNumClustStand == 0)
  PreSetNumClustStand <- optimalClustNum(ClustInd, method="FCM")
#### Visualize
  estimClust.plot(ClustInd)

#### Run clustering (VSClust and standard fcm clustering
ClustOut <- runClustWrapper(dat, 
                            PreSetNumClustVSClust, 
                            NULL, 
                            VSClust=TRUE, 
                            scaling="standardize",
                            cores=cores)
Bestcl <- ClustOut$Bestcl
VSClust_cl <- Bestcl

## Write clustering results (VSClust)
write.csv(data.frame(cluster=Bestcl$cluster,
                     ClustOut$outFileClust,
                     isClusterMember=rowMaxs(Bestcl$membership)>0.5,
                     maxMembership=rowMaxs(Bestcl$membership),
                     Bestcl$membership), 
          paste(Experiment, 
                "FCMVarMResults", 
                Sys.Date(), 
                ".csv", 
                sep=""))
## Write coordinates of cluster centroids
write.csv(Bestcl$centers, 
          paste(Experiment,
                "FCMVarMResultsCentroids",
                Sys.Date(), 
                ".csv", 
                sep=""))

# Functional enrichment
# Note: requires network access to the STRING API; skipped when unavailable
ClustEnriched <- tryCatch(
    runFuncEnrich(VSClust_cl, infosource = "KEGG"),
    error = function(e) {
        message("STRING enrichment unavailable: ", conditionMessage(e))
        NULL
    }
)

# Take the reduce version of the enrichment (redFuncs), not the full one 
# (fullFuncs)
redClustEnriched <- ClustEnriched$redFuncs

# Load the clusterProfiler package
library(clusterProfiler)

# Plot the top 10 most enriched KEGG pathways
dotplot(redClustEnriched, showCategory=10, title="KEGG enrichment", size = "count")
